name: IN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -13 point partisan lean
Incumbent Rudy Yakym has a large fundraising advantage ($5.2M raised)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about 4%
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The district's -13 point Republican lean, Yakym's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing him near 97% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline with a slightly wider margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected scandal shifting the fundamentals could narrow the margin, but the structural Republican advantage is unlikely to change.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Indiana's 2nd District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Rudy Yakym is seeking another term after winning the seat in 2022. He has raised over $5 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Jamee Decio, who has raised about $356,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Yakym's incumbency and financial edge, and prediction markets that give Democrats only a small chance. The forecast expects Yakym to win by roughly sixteen points, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
